message.content:
You are auditing ONE CUDA kernel header on a real NVIDIA H100 (sm_90a) build of the SuperGrok1.5 repo (cwd /workspace/SuperGrok1.5). The extension already builds, links, imports, and 10/11 optimizers run; you are hunting LATENT on-device correctness bugs (especially on code paths the grokking race does not exercise, and numeric errors).

Files to read:
 - grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/adamw_sm90.cuh   (THE kernel)
 - its canonical optimizer math: csrc/algorithms/adamw.h            (compare the device math against this, if applicable)
 - the binding that calls it: grep csrc/bindings/bindings.cpp for the relevant launch_/op name to see the Python->C++ dtype/shape contract.
 - Optionally the Python optimizer grokking_optimizers/optimizers/adamw.py to see what dtypes/shapes it actually passes.


KNOWN BUG CLASSES already confirmed on this H100 (look for MORE of the same):
 (A) Mixed-dtype paired tensors into a single-template kernel: the kernel
     dispatches on ONE tensor's scalar_type() (e.g. weight) then reads a PAIRED
     tensor (e.g. its bias) with data_ptr<SAME_T>(). If Python can pass them in
     different dtypes (weight bf16 via projection_precision='bf16', bias left
     fp32) -> "expected BFloat16 but found Float" at runtime. (Confirmed: SG2
     input_proj_W bf16 vs input_proj_b fp32.)
 (B) Wrong count/loop-bound: a kernel loops 't < n_tasks' or indexes arr[t]
     where n_tasks / the size were set to the ELEMENT count instead of the
     TASK/entry count, walking a small array out of bounds. (Confirmed: fused_step
     n_tasks=n.)
 (C) at:: host ops mixing bf16 weights with fp32 activations without a .to()
     coercion (e.g. a.matmul(b) where a is bf16 and b fp32).
 (D) reshape/view({-1, K}) where the tensor numel may not be divisible by K
     (dimension-wiring mismatch between the passed config int and the actual
     tensor shape). (Confirmed: SG2 meta-net '[-1,44]' vs numel 192.)
 (E) Missing __syncthreads()/__syncwarp() between dependent shared-memory phases,
     or a grid/block index that can exceed the allocated buffer.
 (F) Numeric divergence from the canonical algorithm header (wrong formula,
     swapped operands, missing bias-correction, wrong beta, etc.).


Method: read the kernel fully. For every kernel that dispatches on a tensor dtype, check that ALL tensors it reads with data_ptr<T>() under that branch are guaranteed that dtype. For every reshape/index, check the dimension is derivable and divides. For optimizer kernels, verify the per-element update matches the canonical header formula EXACTLY (operand order, bias-correction, eps placement). 

Report ONLY findings you can back with a specific code snippet and a concrete reachability argument. Prefer precision over recall: a 'certain' high-severity finding is worth far more than ten speculative ones. If the kernel looks correct, return an empty findings array — that is a valid, valuable result. Return the structured object.

49	using ::sg::algorithms::adamw_step;

51	
52	// Minimum resident blocks/SM for the bandwidth-bound element-wise applies.
53	// Caps registers so occupancy stays high on the memory-bound path.
54	#ifndef SG_ADAMW_MIN_BLOCKS
55	#define SG_ADAMW_MIN_BLOCKS 4
56	#endif
57	
58	// =========================================================================
59	//  Scalar grid-stride kernel. SG_TUNED_UNROLL elements per iteration; the
60	//  canonical adamw_step is CALLED (math single-sourced) — the unroll only
61	//  changes the loop structure the autotuner generates, not the math.
62	// =========================================================================
63	
64	template <typename ParamT, typename GradT, int UNROLL>
65	__global__ void __launch_bounds__(SG_TUNED_BLOCK_SIZE, SG_ADAMW_MIN_BLOCKS)
66	adamw_kernel(
67	    ParamT* param, float* exp_avg, float* exp_avg_sq,
68	    const GradT* grad,
69	    float lr, float beta1, float beta2, float eps, float wd,
70	    float bc1, float bc2, int64_t N
71	) {
72	    const int64_t stride = prim::grid_stride() * UNROLL;
73	    const int64_t base0 = prim::grid_stride_index() * UNROLL;
74	    for (int64_t base = base0; base < N; base += stride) {
75	        #pragma unroll
76	        for (int u = 0; u < UNROLL; ++u) {
77	            const int64_t i = base + u;
78	            if (i < N) {
79	                SG_SANITIZE_GRAD_INPLACE(grad, i);
80	                adamw_step(param, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, grad,
81	                           lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, i);
82	            }
83	        }
84	    }
85	}
86	
87	// =========================================================================
88	//  FP32 vec4 fast path (when param, grad, both states are FP32 and 16B-aligned)
89	// =========================================================================
90	
91	__global__ void __launch_bounds__(SG_TUNED_BLOCK_SIZE, SG_ADAMW_MIN_BLOCKS)
92	adamw_kernel_vec4_fp32(
93	    float4* param4, float4* exp_avg4, float4* exp_avg_sq4,
94	    const float4* grad4,
95	    float lr, float beta1, float beta2, float eps, float wd,
96	    float bc1, float bc2, int64_t N4
97	) {
98	    const int64_t stride = prim::grid_stride();
99	    for (int64_t i = prim::grid_stride_index(); i < N4; i += stride) {
100	        SG_SANITIZE_GRAD4_INPLACE(grad4, i);
101	        adamw_step_vec4(param4, exp_avg4, exp_avg_sq4, grad4,
102	                        lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, i);
103	    }
104	}
105

107	//  Host-side launcher (per-tensor)
108	// =========================================================================
109	
110	void launch_adamw_step(
111	    torch::Tensor& param,
112	    torch::Tensor& exp_avg,
113	    torch::Tensor& exp_avg_sq,
114	    const torch::Tensor& grad,
115	    float lr, float beta1, float beta2, float eps, float wd,
116	    float bc1, float bc2
117	) {
118	    const int64_t N = param.numel();
119	    if (N == 0) return;
120	
121	    auto stream = at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream().stream();
122	    const int block = SG_TUNED_BLOCK_SIZE;
123	    // Clamp the grid in int64 (N can exceed 2^31) then cast the grid dim to int
124	    // (grid dims are int; the element index inside the kernel is int64_t).
125	    const int grid = static_cast<int>(
126	        std::min<int64_t>(65535, (N + block - 1) / block));
127	
128	    // §6.1: keep the Adam moments (m, v) L2-resident across the step.
129	    prim::L2PersistScope l2(stream,
130	        exp_avg.data_ptr(), exp_avg.nbytes(),
131	        exp_avg_sq.data_ptr(), exp_avg_sq.nbytes());
132	
133	    const bool all_fp32 = param.scalar_type() == torch::kFloat32 &&
134	                          grad.scalar_type() == torch::kFloat32;
135	
136	    if (SG_TUNED_VEC_WIDTH == 4 && all_fp32 &&
137	        prim::is_vec4_alignable(param.data_ptr(), N) &&
138	        prim::is_vec4_alignable(grad.data_ptr(), N)) {
139	        const int64_t N4 = N / 4;
140	        const int grid4 = static_cast<int>(
141	            std::min<int64_t>(65535, (N4 + block - 1) / block));
142	        adamw_kernel_vec4_fp32<<<grid4, block, 0, stream>>>(
143	            reinterpret_cast<float4*>(param.data_ptr<float>()),
144	            reinterpret_cast<float4*>(exp_avg.data_ptr<float>()),
145	            reinterpret_cast<float4*>(exp_avg_sq.data_ptr<float>()),
146	            reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(grad.data_ptr<float>()),
147	            lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, N4);
148	        SG_LAUNCH_CHECK(stream);
149	        return;
150	    }
151	
152	    AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND2(
153	        at::ScalarType::Half, at::ScalarType::BFloat16,
154	        param.scalar_type(), "adamw_step", [&] {
155	            adamw_kernel<scalar_t, scalar_t, SG_TUNED_UNROLL>
156	                <<<grid, block, 0, stream>>>(
157	                param.data_ptr<scalar_t>(),
158	                exp_avg.data_ptr<float>(),
159	                exp_avg_sq.data_ptr<float>(),
160	                grad.data_ptr<scalar_t>(),
161	                lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, N);
162	            SG_LAUNCH_CHECK(stream);
163	        });
164	}

1	"""
2	AdamW — Adam with decoupled weight decay (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2017).
3	
4	Per-element update (FP32 accumulator, BF16/FP16 storage allowed):
5	
6	    m_t = beta1 * m_{t-1} + (1 - beta1) * g
7	    v_t = beta2 * v_{t-1} + (1 - beta2) * g^2
8	    bc1 = 1 - beta1^t                                # un-inverted
9	    bc2 = 1 - beta2^t                                # un-inverted
10	    m_hat = m_t / bc1
11	    v_hat = v_t / bc2
12	    p_{t+1} = p_t - lr * (m_hat / (sqrt(v_hat) + eps) + wd * p_t)
13	
14	All computation is dispatched to the fused C++/CUDA kernel via _ops.
15	Math: csrc/algorithms/adamw.h. Launchers:
16	  csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/launch_adamw.cu
17	  csrc/backends/hip/gfx942/launch_adamw.hip.cpp
18	  csrc/backends/pallas/launch_adamw.py
19	"""
20	
21	from typing import Iterable, Optional, Tuple
22	
23	import torch
24	from torch import Tensor
25	from torch.optim.optimizer import Optimizer
26	
27	from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import get_ops
28	
29	_ops = get_ops()  # Fails loudly on first attribute access if extension not built
30	
31	
32	def _validate_grad(p):
33	    """Validate a gradient before handing its data_ptr to the fused kernel.
34	
35	    The fused kernels index raw contiguous memory and dispatch on the
36	    parameter's dtype (treating the grad buffer as the same scalar type),
37	    so a sparse, dtype-mismatched, or non-contiguous gradient would
38	    silently corrupt the parameter and optimizer state. There is no Python
39	    fallback, so reject the unsupported cases loudly and densify the rest.
40	    """
41	    g = p.grad
42	    if g.is_sparse:
43	        raise RuntimeError(
44	            "fused optimizer kernel does not support sparse gradients")
45	    if g.dtype != p.dtype:
46	        raise RuntimeError(
47	            f"grad dtype {g.dtype} != param dtype {p.dtype}; cast gradients "
48	            "to the parameter dtype before step()")
49	    return g if g.is_contiguous() else g.contiguous()
50	
51	
52	class AdamW(Optimizer):
53	    """Adam with decoupled weight decay (multi-tensor fused step).
54	
55	    Args:
56	        params: Iterable of parameters or parameter groups.
57	        lr: Learning rate (default: 1e-3).
58	        betas: (beta1, beta2) for the first/second moment EMAs
59	            (default: (0.9, 0.999)).
60	        eps: Numerical stabiliser added to the denominator (default: 1e-8).
61	        weight_decay: Decoupled weight decay coefficient (default: 1e-2).
62	        use_grad_hooks: When True, register
63	            ``register_post_accumulate_grad_hook`` on each parameter so the
64	            update runs while gradients are still L2-warm (requires
65	            PyTorch >= 2.1).
66	    """
67	
68	    def __init__(
69	        self,
70	        params: Iterable,
71	        lr: float = 1e-3,
72	        betas: Tuple[float, float] = (0.9, 0.999),
73	        eps: float = 1e-8,
74	        weight_decay: float = 1e-2,
75	        use_grad_hooks: bool = False,
76	    ) -> None:
77	        if lr < 0.0:
78	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid learning rate: {lr}")
79	        if not isinstance(betas, (tuple, list)) or len(betas) != 2:
80	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid betas (expected a 2-tuple): {betas}")
81	        if not 0.0 <= betas[0] < 1.0:
82	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid beta parameter at index 0: {betas[0]}")
83	        if not 0.0 <= betas[1] < 1.0:
84	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid beta parameter at index 1: {betas[1]}")
85	        if eps < 0.0:
86	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid epsilon: {eps}")
87	        if weight_decay < 0.0:
88	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid weight_decay: {weight_decay}")
89	
90	        defaults = dict(lr=lr, betas=betas, eps=eps, weight_decay=weight_decay)
91	        super().__init__(params, defaults)
92	
93	        # Per-group cache of the static tensor lists handed to the fused kernel.
94	        # Params and their state buffers keep a fixed identity across steps, so
95	        # we build params/exp_avg/exp_avg_sq once (avoiding the per-step
96	        # self.state[p] re-hash and list rebuilds) and only refresh the dynamic
97	        # grads_list + step counters. Invalidated by add_param_group.
98	        self._static_cache: dict = {}
99	        # Lazily-bound fused kernel callable (resolved once at first step()).
100	        self._fused_step = None
101	
102	        self._use_grad_hooks = use_grad_hooks
103	        if use_grad_hooks:
104	            _register_grad_hooks(self)
105	
106	    def add_param_group(self, param_group) -> None:
107	        # Static tensor lists are derived from the param groups; drop the cache
108	        # so the next step() rebuilds them.
109	        self._static_cache = {}
110	        super().add_param_group(param_group)
111	
112	    def _group_cache(self, group):
113	        """Return cached (params, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, step_counts) for *group*.
114	
115	        The cache is keyed on the tuple of grad-bearing parameter ids; if that
116	        set changes (a param newly receives or loses a grad) the cache is
117	        rebuilt so semantics match the original per-step scan exactly.
118	        """
119	        key = tuple(id(p) for p in group["params"] if p.grad is not None)
120	        cached = self._static_cache.get(id(group))
121	        if cached is not None and cached[0] == key:
122	            return cached[1]
123	
124	        params_list = []
125	        exp_avg_list = []
126	        exp_avg_sq_list = []
127	        step_counts = []  # mutable per-param step counters (1-element lists)
128	        for p in group["params"]:
129	            if p.grad is None:
130	                continue
131	            state = self.state[p]
132	            if len(state) == 0:
133	                state["step"] = 0
134	                state["exp_avg"] = torch.zeros_like(p, dtype=torch.float32)
135	                state["exp_avg_sq"] = torch.zeros_like(p, dtype=torch.float32)
136	            params_list.append(p)
137	            exp_avg_list.append(state["exp_avg"])
138	            exp_avg_sq_list.append(state["exp_avg_sq"])
139	            step_counts.append(state)
140	        entry = (params_list, exp_avg_list, exp_avg_sq_list, step_counts)
141	        self._static_cache[id(group)] = (key, entry)
142	        return entry
143	
144	    @torch.no_grad()

70	    unsigned threshold = rand_bits & 0xFFFF; // random 16-bit threshold
71	    if (truncated > threshold) {
